title: Add UNIQUE(character_id) to active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state so state upserts work
description:
State upserts fail at runtime: the DAL saves for active buffs, spell slots and the round counter use `ON CONFLICT(character_id) DO UPDATE`, but migration 003_state.sql creates active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state with only `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` and no UNIQUE constraint on character_id. SQLite rejects every such upsert with "ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint". Desired: each of the three tables holds at most one row per character, and the existing upserts work unchanged.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12, autonomous; supervisor-confirmed evidence)
- Fix in the schema, not in the queries: add a NEW migration (next number after 005); never edit 003.
- The migration first dedupes existing rows per character_id, keeping the row with the highest id (the latest write), then adds a UNIQUE index on character_id for active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state.
- Remove the 9 `t.Skip("bug: upserts use ON CONFLICT(character_id) ...")` DAL tests added by critical-518.3 (PR #13, branch feat/518.3-backfill-tests) in buffdal (7) and spelldal (2) tests. Hence blocked by critical-518.3: stack on that branch or start after it is merged.
- NOT in scope: the nat-1 / nat-20 `t.Skip("bug?: ...")` in combatsvc tests (separate rules decision, handled by the supervisor with the user).

## Current behaviour
SaveActiveBuffs, SaveSlots and SaveRoundNumber always fail, which breaks Activate / Dismiss / Trigger buff, Next Round, Cast spell and Reset slots. Reproduced live (dev-518-6): POST /api/spells/0/cast on a fresh DB -> 500 "save slots: upsert spell_slots: ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint".

## Key interfaces
- New migration file under the sqlite migrations dir, e.g. `006_state_unique_character.sql`: per table `DELETE FROM <t> WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM <t> GROUP BY character_id);` then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS <t>_character_id_uq ON <t>(character_id);`.
- The migration runner splits files on semicolons and executes statements one by one (no wrapping transaction), recording the file in schema_migrations only after all succeed: keep every statement idempotent and free of semicolons inside literals/comments.
- DAL query files (buffs.sql, spells.sql) and the BuffStore / spell-slot store ports stay unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New migration exists; 001-005 are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [ ] On a fresh DB, SaveActiveBuffs, SaveSlots and SaveRoundNumber succeed on first insert AND on a second save for the same character (row updated, still exactly one row).
- [ ] On a DB that already holds duplicate rows per character_id in any of the three tables, migrating keeps only the highest-id row per character and then creates the unique index (covered by a test that seeds duplicates before applying the new migration, or an equivalent migrate test).
- [ ] Re-running migrations on an already-migrated DB is a no-op (no error).
- [ ] The 9 buffdal/spelldal `t.Skip("bug: upserts use ON CONFLICT ...")` tests are un-skipped and pass.
- [ ] `just generate` run; any change in generated bob output (models/factory/queries) committed, and the CI generated-code check passes.
- [ ] Manual or HTTP-level check: POST /api/spells/0/cast on a fresh DB no longer returns 500.
- [ ] `just validate` passes.

## Tests
buffdal and spelldal DAL tests (the 9 un-skipped ones), plus a migration test for the dedupe-then-index path on pre-existing duplicates.

## Risky
Yes: migration on existing data (deletes duplicate rows) and buff / spell-slot / round-counter state semantics. Needs review per the workflow doc ("Migrations and DAL", "State integrity").

## Parallelism
Adds a migration touching active_buffs, spell_slots, round_state: do not run in parallel with another item adding a migration on those tables or changing bob generated output.

## Out of scope
- Changing the upsert queries or the store ports.
- The nat-1 / nat-20 combat skips.
- Merging the three tables or moving state into the characters table.

title: Decide fly.io hosting shape: access control, topology, backups
description:
Decisions needed before any fly.io work. The PRD says 'no authentication, Tailscale is the security boundary'; a public fly.io URL breaks that.

Questions for the user:
1. Access control: (a) shared-secret/basic auth at the edge, (b) fly private networking + WireGuard/Tailscale only (no public ingress), (c) real login. Recommendation: (a) or (b); the app has no user model and is a single-character personal tool.
2. Topology: one container where the Go API also serves the built web assets (simplest on fly: one machine, one volume), vs. separate api and nginx apps as in docker-compose. Recommendation: single container.
3. SQLite on fly: single machine + fly volume (no horizontal scale, which is fine). Backup via fly volume snapshots only, or Litestream to object storage? Recommendation: snapshots first, Litestream if the data matters.
4. Environments: production only, or also a staging app deployed from PRs?
5. Budget/region constraints.

Output: decisions recorded in this bead's notes and in docs/ (an ADR-style note), then the dependent beads are un-labelled needs-info.

title: Rulebooks reference: PHB + DMG as agent-readable docs in a private repo
description:
The user's request (2026-10-13, verbatim): "we should have the phb and the dmg in the repo in documentation in a format suitable for agents to refer to. ideally with some kind of indexing to avoid wasting tokens. what do you propose." Sources: https://archive.org/details/player-s-handbook-2nd-edition-2101 and https://archive.org/details/add2nddungeonmastersguidetsr2100

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- ceffo/critical is PUBLIC and the books are WotC copyright, so no rules text goes into critical. The converted text lives in a separate PRIVATE repo, ceffo/critical-rulebooks.
- critical worktrees reach it through a sibling clone at the fixed path ~/code/critical-rulebooks (no submodule: `git worktree add` doesn't init submodules). critical gets only a `just rulebooks` recipe and a pointer in AGENTS.md / docs/agent-workflow.md.
- The supervisor creates the repo (`gh repo create ceffo/critical-rulebooks --private`) and pushes the private repo's work straight to its `main` after its `check` passes. No PRs in the private repo. The critical item is a normal PR.
- The raw archive.org OCR (`*_djvu.txt`, plus the PHB `_page_numbers.json`) is committed under source/. PDFs are fetched on demand by a script, never committed.
- INDEX.md: one line per chapter/section/spell/table PLUS every entry from both printed book indexes, each resolved to `term | book p.N | path`. Agents grep it, never read it whole.
- No seed-shaped spell export: the vodabois scrape stays the app's spell catalog source of truth. PHB spell files carry their stat block as frontmatter only.
- Books in scope: the PHB and DMG only. The layout takes another <book>/ later without rework.
- Not MVP (Saturday hard cut): P3, outside critical-qki.

## Private repo gate (instead of `just validate`)
A `check` script in critical-rulebooks: rerunning the conversion gives byte-identical output; every path in INDEX.md exists; every printed-index page resolves to a file; spot terms ("surprise", "THAC0", "Magic Missile") each give at least one INDEX line.

## Children
1 repo + script + sections + INDEX; 2 per-spell files; 3 hand-checked tables; 4 critical pointer + recipe.

title: Create critical-rulebooks: OCR source, conversion script, PHB/DMG section files, INDEX.md with the printed indexes
description:
Create the private repo ceffo/critical-rulebooks and a reproducible conversion of the PHB and DMG (archive.org OCR) into section-sized Markdown files with a grep-able INDEX.md. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
See the parent epic. The supervisor runs `gh repo create ceffo/critical-rulebooks --private`, clones it to ~/code/critical-rulebooks and gives the developer a worktree of it. The developer commits there and the supervisor pushes to main once `check` passes (no PR).

## Current behaviour
Nothing exists. Supervisor's sample of the archive.org `*_djvu.txt` OCR (PHB ~1.5 MB, DMG ~1.2 MB): the prose is clean. Problems: line-break hyphenation ("unerr- ingly"), stray quotes ("Tenser’'s"), running headers/footers and page numbers inline, tables mangled. Both books have a printed index (term -> page). The PHB item also has `_page_numbers.json`.

## Key interfaces

title: Actor: remove db field, make pure value type
description:
Actor currently stores *sql.DB internally (actor.go:13), coupling the domain entity to persistence. Every Actor method (TakeDamage, GetHPState, ApplyBuff, etc.) is a thin wrapper that re-passes the same db to package-level functions.

Fix: remove the db field from Actor. LoadActor returns a plain struct with no DB reference. Callers (handlers) call the package-level domain functions directly — no Actor intermediary needed for persistence. Actor methods that are now pure (ApplyBuff, DismissBuff, TriggerBuff) keep their in-memory logic but drop the SaveActiveBuffs call; persistence is the caller's responsibility.

No new interface. No new abstraction. Just delete the field and its wrappers.

Files: api/internal/domain/actor.go, api/internal/handlers/*.go, api/internal/domain/buff_actor_test.go

title: ResolveAttack: pre-aggregate modifiers, decouple from Actor
description:
engine.ResolveAttack (combat.go) reaches into actor.ActiveBuffs mid-calculation to apply modifiers. This means: (a) buff state can diverge between LoadActor and the call, (b) the function does hit resolution + damage + crit + buff aggregation in one 60-line god function with no seam.

Fix: introduce a CombatContext value (pre-computed attack bonus, damage formula, crit threshold, buff modifiers). ResolveAttack takes CombatContext + DiceRoller, returns CombatResult — pure function. The caller (handler or a thin builder) aggregates modifiers before calling. engine/buffs.go ApplyBuffModifiers already produces BuffModifiers; caller computes CombatContext from actor.Stats + BuffModifiers.

Benefit: engine is independently testable without a DB-backed actor. Buff aggregation changes don't touch combat.go.

Files: api/internal/engine/combat.go, api/internal/engine/buffs.go, api/internal/handlers/combat.go

title: Handler boilerplate: extract CharacterContext value struct
description:
Seven handler structs each repeat {DB *sql.DB, CharacterID int64}. This is accidental width — the same pair exists by coincidence, not design.

Fix: introduce a CharacterContext struct (db, characterID) that handlers embed. Constructor: NewCharacterContext(db, charID). Handlers become e.g. type HPHandler struct { CharacterContext }. main.go creates one CharacterContext and embeds it into all handlers.

No interface. No behavioral change. Eliminates the repeated field pair and makes main.go construction obvious.

Files: api/internal/handlers/*.go, api/main.go

title: SaveCategory: move from engine to domain, decouple HTTP from engine types
description:
engine.SaveCategory is defined in api/internal/engine/saves.go but used directly in the HTTP request struct in handlers/rolls.go:21. This leaks engine internals into the HTTP contract — renaming or restructuring SaveCategory would break the API.

Fix: define a SaveCategory string type (or reuse engine's constants) in the domain package. The handler decodes the domain type; engine.ResolveSavingThrow accepts the domain type or the handler translates domain → engine before calling. The HTTP contract is decoupled from engine internals.

Files: api/internal/engine/saves.go, api/internal/handlers/rolls.go, api/internal/domain/types.go

description:
Replace the item kinds (ammo / charged / consumable) with ONE item model whose only real difference is how its count behaves, and turn the Items tab into an Inventory tab with − / + counts. Adding/editing/removing items and weapons are follow-up items.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- User: "these are all consumables... i don't see your point of splitting them between ammo, charges and consumables. it's just their type." An item = name, free-text **type** label (arrows, flask, wand, gem...), count, optional note, optional mechanics the app handles when filled (effect dice, effect save, **magical bonus** +N, **ammo kind**).
- Count behaviour (user confirmed the table):
  - **stock** (arrows, fire flasks): − and + at the table (use, buy more); stays listed at 0, restockable.
  - **charges** (wand of lightning): − only ("i cannot add charges to a wand"); at 0 the item is gone (removed, logged; voiding the use brings it back).
  - **daily** (Power Gem dispel 1/day): − only; stays at 0; refilled to its daily number at long rest only (not by time fast-forward).
- Ammo: linked to weapons by ammo kind (a bow fires "arrow"; every arrow item with ammo kind "arrow" is offered). The arrow's magical bonus adds to to-hit and damage; one is spent per attack, hit or miss. This already works since critical-qki.7 and must keep working.
- The +N is labelled "Magical bonus" (FR "Bonus magique"), shown "+2".
- Tab named "Inventory" (FR "Inventaire"). Every count change is logged and voidable.

- Attack resolver reads magical bonus/ammo kind from the new model (no behaviour change).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Inventory tab lists all items (name, type, count, behaviour badge); − uses one; + exists only on stock items and adds one (logged).
- [ ] A wand used down to 0 disappears; voiding that use brings it back with 1 charge.
- [ ] Arrows at 0 stay listed and can be restocked; the attack picker offers only arrows with count > 0.
- [ ] Long rest refills the gem (daily) and nothing else.
- [ ] Existing DB migrates without loss (test on a DB with the old rows); fresh seed works.
- [ ] Attack with Short Bow +2 and Arrows +1 still adds both to hit and damage and spends one arrow (existing tests pass unchanged in meaning).
- [ ] Go tests (behaviours, removal + void, restock rejection, long rest), migration test, Vitest, e2e step. `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Adding/editing/removing items (next item) and weapons (separate item); encumbrance; prices.

title: Log saving throws and adjust the latest save on its result card
description:
Saving throws become logged table actions, and the latest save can be adjusted after the roll on its result card: the adjustment changes the outcome, never the d20. Origin: the Bard's "Gaia" fire/lightning protections (+4 to saves vs fire/lightning) and any bonus only known after the roll.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- No special code for Gaia: the protections are ordinary buffs the user adds (see the saved-buffs item); the +4 is applied through this adjustment. No damage types and no arithmetic on damage taken: the HP amount entered is final ("value is after all modifiers; the DM does not always disclose what affected it"). The old ideas (halve fire damage, +4 save display) are dropped.
- "Each save throw should have an optional adjustment on the result card. Adjusting it changes the outcome but not the roll."
- "Everything affecting the game should be logged": a save is an action-log entry (category, d20, buff modifiers, target, pass/fail); voidable from the log like other entries.
- Adjustment = one signed integer with − / + buttons, starting at 0, plus an optional reason (e.g. "Gaia fire"); the log line shows it ("adjusted +4 Gaia fire: FAILED → PASSED").
- Only the latest roll's card is adjustable; older entries are fixed with void + reroll. No reminder line of conditional buff bonuses on the card (active buffs are visible in the buff strip).

## Current behaviour
`POST /api/saves` (combathdl.RollSave -> combatsvc.ResolveSavingThrow) rolls d20 + buff SaveBonus vs the category target and returns a RollResult; nothing is logged. The save result card (ResultCard SaveResult) shows the verdict, d20, target, margin, modifiers. `POST /api/log/{id}/amend` exists for hp_change entries only.

## Key interfaces

title: Playwright e2e harness: just e2e on a throwaway stack, with smoke specs and docs

- Local only: no CI job yet (separate P3 item under critical-8g1). `just validate` unchanged; `just e2e` is a separate recipe.

- i18n: flow specs run in en; ONE fr smoke spec toggles to French and checks no raw keys are visible.
- Data: the repo's real `seeds/` + a fresh temp SQLite DB per spec file. Specs assert relative changes (HP drops by the damage entered), never hard-coded character values, so the qki.2 reseed does not break them.
- Selectors: getByRole/getByLabel with English accessible names first; `data-testid` only for non-semantic regions (HP value, log entries).
- Artifacts: HTML report, PNGs and traces in `web/e2e-results/` (gitignored); nothing binary committed. The supervisor relays PNG paths to the user.

## Current behaviour
Agents stop at typecheck/build (+ vitest units after qki.1); nobody can verify a panel headlessly; the supervisor tells the user "look at it yourself". ## Key interfaces
- `just e2e` (from repo root): builds the API, installs/uses Playwright Chromium, runs the suite; any extra args pass through to `playwright test` (e.g. `just e2e smoke.spec.ts`). A `just e2e-install` (or equivalent first-run step) installs the browser.

- A shared fixture that gives each spec file its own stack: API on a free port with a new temp DB under the OS temp dir and `CRITICAL_SEEDS_DIR` = repo `seeds/`, plus a Vite server on a free port whose `/api` proxy targets that API (the proxy target is fixed at Vite start, so either Vite per spec file too or an equivalent that keeps isolation). - [ ] Each spec saves at least one PNG at 1440x900; a deliberately failing assertion leaves a trace zip in `web/e2e-results/`.
- [ ] `web/e2e-results/` and Playwright caches are gitignored; `just validate` does not run e2e and still passes (lint/typecheck include the e2e TS files without breaking).
- [ ] docs/agent-workflow.md updated: "Validation" (UI items must add/extend specs per UI acceptance flow and run `just e2e` green; list screenshot paths in the report), "Running the app for acceptance checks" (`just e2e`, artifacts location), "Review" (visual review uses the e2e screenshots); keep headings stable.

The smoke specs themselves; `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
CI job (separate item under critical-8g1); pixel-diff baselines; vitest component tests; specs for the redesign (qki.6 writes its own and may replace the smoke specs' selectors).

Blocked by critical-qki.1 (the fr smoke needs the language toggle; both edit web/package.json). Blocks critical-qki.6. Model: Sonnet (tooling, not a UI-heavy bead). Not risky per the review triggers.

title: Correct the target AC on the latest attack after the roll
description:
At the table the target's AC is often only known (or corrected by the DM) after the attack is rolled. Let the user correct the target AC on the latest attack's result card: hit/miss and crit are recomputed with the SAME d20 and d100, and the logged attack is amended.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- "Same mechanic will be needed for adjusting the target AC in combat. It is not always known in advance." (same pattern as the save adjustment, critical-qki.14).
- Damage dice are rolled on EVERY attack, even a miss, and stored, so a miss turned into a hit shows its damage without rerolling (user: yes).
- The logged attack entry is amended to the new AC and outcome, audited like an HP amend (user: yes). "Everything affecting the game should be logged."
- Only the latest roll's card is adjustable; older entries: void + reroll.

## Current behaviour
combatsvc.ResolveAttack: needed = EffectiveThac0 − TargetAC; Hit = d20 ≥ needed; IsCrit when d20 − d100 ≥ needed (multiplier from the house crit table); damage dice are rolled only on a hit. The attack is logged (kind `attack`, with ammo snapshots). The attack card shows the target AC read-only.

## Key interfaces
- ResolveAttack always rolls the damage dice and stores them in the result/log payload (shown only on a hit).
- Correct: e.g. `POST /api/log/{id}/adjust` with `{targetAc:int}` for `attack` entries (reuse the endpoint shape from qki.14); the server recomputes hit, margin, crit (row lookup with the stored d100), and damage from the stored dice and stored modifiers; records an audited correction; returns the updated RollResult. Ammo is NOT spent again. Rejected when not the latest roll, voided or not an attack.
- The attack card's target AC becomes an editable number field (− / +); the heading/verdict/damage update from the server response.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A miss vs AC 5 (d20 11, needed 13) becomes a hit when the AC is corrected to 7; damage shown is the dice rolled at attack time (no reroll; dice port called once per attack).
- [ ] A hit can become a miss (damage hidden), and a crit can appear/disappear from the stored d100 per the crit table; nat 1 / nat 20 rules unchanged.
- [ ] The log entry shows "AC 5 → 7: MISS → HIT" and the new damage; voiding it still restores ammo as today.
- [ ] Ammo count unchanged by the correction.
- [ ] Go table-driven tests (miss→hit, hit→miss, crit flip, damage reuse, rejections) that fail on the old code; Vitest for the card; e2e step. `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Adjusting other modifiers after the roll (situational stays pre-roll); adjusting from the combat log; HP of the target.

Risky: yes (rules math: hit/crit/damage; log correction semantics). Model: Opus. Not blocked by qki.14 but touches the same result card and log correction code: run after it, reusing its endpoint pattern.

title: Buff notes and saved buffs for one-click re-adding
description:
Make adding buffs fast: a free-text note on every buff, and saved buffs re-added with one click. This covers the Bard's "Gaia" fire/lightning protections and the Power Gem forms (critical-qki.15, closed as covered by this) with no special-cased code.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- User: "let's make it that we can add buffs easily"; no special handling for Gaia or the Power Gem forms.
- Note: a free-text note on a buff (e.g. "+4 saves vs fire, damage −50%"), shown on the buff badge (hover/click); editable later through the buff's Edit button; the change is logged.
- Saved buffs: a "Save for reuse" checkbox in the Add buff form stores the buff as a template (name, rounds, charges, effects, note). The top of the Add form shows the saved buffs as chips; a click FILLS the form (still editable, e.g. rounds), then Add. Each chip has a × to delete the saved buff; deleting is logged.
- "Remove all hardcoded stuff": no saved buffs are seeded; the list starts empty.
- Power Gem forms become user-made saved buffs, e.g. thunder hammer = weapon_buff 5, min_str 18, spells_buff 2 (double damage dice, stacks with the crit multiplier per the existing formula; user: yes), note "thunderclap stuns 30 m".

## Current behaviour
BuffStrip has an Add buff form (name, rounds left, charges left, effect rows from BUFF_EFFECT_KEYS) and an Edit form (rounds/charges only). `POST /api/buffs`, `PATCH /api/buffs/{id}`, `DELETE /api/buffs/{id}`; every change is a `buff_change` log entry with a `buffs` snapshot, voidable. No note, no templates.

## Key interfaces
- BuffEffect gains `Note string`; BuffEdit gains `Note *string`. Persisted (migration) and part of the `buffs` snapshot so void restores it.
- Saved buff template: own table (migration), e.g. `saved_buffs(id, name, duration, charges, effects json, note, created_at)`. Endpoints e.g. `GET /api/buffs/saved`, `POST /api/buffs/saved`, `DELETE /api/buffs/saved/{id}`; create/delete logged (new log kind or buff_change with its own snapshot key + restorer, so void works).
- Activating from a template is the normal `POST /api/buffs` (the form sends the filled values); "Save for reuse" = the form also POSTs the template.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Add a buff with a note: the badge shows the note; Edit changes it; both logged; void restores the previous note.
- [ ] Tick "Save for reuse": the template appears as a chip; clicking it fills every field (name, rounds, charges, effects, note); changing rounds then Add creates the buff with the changed rounds.
- [ ] × on a chip deletes the template (logged, voidable); it never touches active buffs.
- [ ] Fresh DB from `seeds/`: no saved buffs.
- [ ] A saved "Power Gem: thunder hammer" (weapon_buff 5, min_str 18, spells_buff 2) gives the expected attack damage (test through the attack resolver: doubled dice, ×crit after).
- [ ] Migration safe on an existing DB; `just generate` output committed; Go service/handler tests, Vitest, e2e step. `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Time fast-forward (separate item); conditional bonuses applied automatically; sharing templates across characters.

Risky: yes (migration; buffs state/snapshots). Model: Sonnet. Not blocked; it adds a migration and log behaviour like qki.14, so don't run it in parallel with qki.14 / the time fast-forward item.

title: Action log: one append-only log of table actions with audited amend/void
description:
One append-only action log records every table action and lets the user amend or void any entry; it becomes the HP ledger and the combat log. Backend + API only; the redesign item builds the UI on it.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- "damage/healing ledger with good ui. should be able to amend/correct a mistake" (user).
- One action log for all actions (HP change, cast, buff change, Next Round, attack, item use), not per-feature undo.
- Each entry stores before/after snapshots of the state it changed (buffs, slots, round, counters). Voiding an entry restores its "before" state when no later non-voided entry changed the same state; otherwise the void is refused with a clear error (or the user voids the later one first).
- Corrections are audited: amend/void are new events pointing at the original; history shows "amended"/"voided". No in-place edits.

## Current behaviour
hp_events ledger with append + "undo last" only; buffs/slots/round are JSON state rows overwritten in place, no history; nothing records attacks or casts.

## Key interfaces
- Action entry: id, character_id, round, kind (hp_change | cast | buff_change | round_advance | attack | item_use | ...), summary payload (JSON, e.g. full RollResult for attacks), before/after state snapshots, created_at, status derived from correction events.
- Correction event: target action id, kind amend|void, new payload for amend (amend on HP changes: amount and source).
- A domain port other services use to record an action atomically with their state write (same transaction).
- Current HP = SUM of effective HP deltas (amended value, voided = 0), still computed in SQL.
- REST: `GET /api/log` (newest first, with correction status), `POST /api/log/{id}/amend`, `POST /api/log/{id}/void`; existing `POST /api/hp/event` now writes through the log; `/api/hp/undo` = void of the last HP entry.
- Existing hp_events data migrated (new migration file, never edit an applied one).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] HP damage/heal recorded as log entries; amend changes current HP and keeps the original visible; void removes its effect.
- [ ] Voiding an entry with snapshots restores the before state; voiding when a later entry changed the same state is refused with `{"error": ...}`.
- [ ] Record + state write are one transaction (test with a failing DAL).
- [ ] Migration applies on an existing dev DB with hp_events data; totals unchanged.
- [ ] Service and DAL tests per docs/backend.md; `just generate` and `just mocks` run; `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Recording casts, rounds, buffs, attacks, items (each feature item plugs into this port); the UI.

Risky: migration + ledger/state semantics.

title: Fast-forward time in decimal hours to expire buffs
description:
Let the user fast-forward game time in decimal hours so long-running buffs count down and expire correctly between fights.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- A "⏩ Time passes" control next to the round controls: the user types decimal hours (0.25, 1.5, 8). 1 round = 1 minute (AD&D), so rounds = floor(hours × 60) (user: round DOWN); the preview "= 90 rounds" shows before confirming.
- Every timed buff loses that many rounds; those reaching 0 expire and show in the usual "expired" notice. Charge-only and untimed buffs are untouched.
- The combat round counter goes to 0 (user: "goes to zero").
- Logged and voidable ("everything affecting the game should be logged").
- Buff badges show hours/minutes for long durations, from 60 rounds up: "150 r · 2 h 30".
- Daily items are NOT refilled by fast-forward (long rest only).

## Current behaviour
buffsvc: Next Round (AdvanceRound) decrements timed buffs by 1 and expires at 0; End combat (ResetRound -> 0) and Set round move the counter and leave buffs alone; all logged with `buffs`/`round` snapshots and restorers. Badges show "N rounds".

## Key interfaces
- buffsvc `PassTime(ctx, characterID, rounds int)` -> (active, expired, round) in one transaction: decrement timed buffs by rounds, expire ≤ 0, round = 0; one log entry (new kind e.g. `time_passed`, payload hours + rounds) with `buffs` and `round` snapshots so void restores both.
- `POST /api/round/pass-time` with `{hours: number}`; the server converts (floor(hours×60)), rejects ≤ 0 or > a sane max (e.g. 720 h) and results of 0 rounds; returns the same shape as Next Round. The preview conversion may be shown client-side but the server is the authority.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] 1.5 h = 90 rounds: a buff with 100 rounds keeps 10, one with 60 expires (notice), a charge-only buff is unchanged; the round counter is 0.
- [ ] 0.01 h is rejected (0 rounds) with a clear message; 0.02 h = 1 round.
- [ ] Voiding the entry restores the buffs and the previous round number.
- [ ] Badge: 150 rounds shows "150 r · 2 h 30"; 59 rounds shows rounds only (FR/EN).
- [ ] Go table-driven tests (conversion floor, expiry edge at exactly 0, untimed/charged untouched, void), handler test, Vitest for the badge format, e2e step. `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
An in-game clock / time of day; refilling daily items; spell slot recovery (long rest exists).

Risky: yes (buff/round state semantics, new log kind). Model: Opus. Not blocked, but adds a log kind in shared code: not in parallel with qki.14, qki.28, qki.29 or the inventory items.

title: Inventory: add, edit and remove items
description:
In the Inventory tab, add a new item (loot, purchase), edit any field of an item, and remove one. Builds on the item model of critical-qki.13.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- At the table the user needs: add loot, remove (sold/broken), edit any field (user: all of these). Inline in the Inventory tab: ✎ and 🗑 per row, "+ Add" opens an inline form.
- Fields: name, type (free text, suggestions from existing types), behaviour (stock / charges / daily), count, daily number (daily only), note, and optional mechanics: effect dice, effect save, magical bonus, ammo kind.

Each writes one log entry with the `items:<id>` snapshot (create/delete restorable by void; a void of a create removes it).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Add "Arrows +3" (stock, ammo kind arrow, magical bonus 3, count 6): it appears in the Inventory and in the Short Bow ammo picker.
- [ ] Edit the wand's charges from 4 to 3: logged; void restores 4.
- [ ] Remove an item: gone from Inventory and pickers; void brings it back with its count.
- [ ] Invalid dice ("2x6"), empty name, negative count are rejected with a message under the field.
- [ ] Go service/handler tests, Vitest, e2e step. `just validate` green.

Weapons (separate item); encumbrance.

Risky: yes (API contract, item state). Model: Sonnet. Blocked by critical-qki.13 (model + tab). Not in parallel with the weapons editor (same tab and log code).

title: Inventory: add, edit and remove weapons
description:

title: Make the SQLite opener wait on locks: busy_timeout 5000 ms and WAL on every connection
description:
The app's SQLite opener sets no busy timeout and uses the default rollback journal, so when two pool connections write (or one writes while another reads) the loser fails at once with SQLITE_BUSY / "database is locked" instead of waiting. With database/sql's multi-connection pool this can happen from ordinary concurrent HTTP requests (the dashboard fires several at once). Make the opener configure every pooled connection so concurrent writers wait and succeed.

Found by dev-qki-5 and its reviewer (2026-10-12): qki.5's concurrency test (PR #26) had to add `_pragma=busy_timeout` to its own DSN to pass.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12, autonomous scoper, no user input)
- Busy timeout 5000 ms on every connection, set by the opener (sqlite.Open), not by callers.
- Journal mode WAL for file-backed databases (readers no longer block the writer). In-memory DSNs cannot use WAL: the opener must keep working for `file::memory:?cache=shared&mode=memory` (used by DAL tests) and for an existing on-disk dev DB.
- Pragmas must apply to every connection the pool opens, not just the first (so: DSN `_pragma=` parameters for modernc.org/sqlite, or an equivalent per-connection hook; a one-off `db.Exec("PRAGMA ...")` after Open is NOT enough for busy_timeout).
- If the caller's DSN already sets a pragma (e.g. qki.5's test), the caller's value wins or the result is equivalent; no duplicate/conflicting pragma error.
- Standalone task, not in epic critical-qki: single user on a laptop, low urgency, cheap.

## Current behaviour
`sqlite.Open(dsn)` calls `sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)` + Ping with nothing else. CRITICAL_DSN defaults to `critical.db` (a bare path; `just dev` uses `../.dev/critical.db`). No busy_timeout, journal_mode or foreign_keys pragma anywhere in non-test code.

## Key interfaces
- `func Open(dsn string) (*DB, error)` in the storage/sqlite package keeps its signature; it normalises the DSN (bare path or `file:` URI) and adds the pragmas.
- `(*DB).InTx` / `WrapTx` / `Conn` unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every pooled connection reports `PRAGMA busy_timeout` = 5000 (test opens several connections, e.g. by holding one with db.Conn and checking another).
- [ ] A file-backed DB opened via Open reports `PRAGMA journal_mode` = wal.
- [ ] Test: two goroutines each run a write transaction (InTx or WrapTx) on the same file DB concurrently, the first holding its tx open briefly; both commit, no SQLITE_BUSY. The test fails on main without the fix.
- [ ] Open still works with a bare path, a `file:` URI with existing query params, and the shared in-memory DSN used by the DAL tests; existing tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] qki.5's concurrency test no longer needs its own `_pragma=busy_timeout` (remove it if PR #26 has merged by then; otherwise leave a note in the PR).
- [ ] `just validate` passes.

## Out of scope
- The hazard of a pool (non-ctx) write issued while an InTx transaction is open on the same request: busy_timeout only turns that into a 5 s wait then an error. If it shows up, file a separate bug to route the write through `sqlite.Conn(ctx, ...)`.
- Connection pool sizing (SetMaxOpenConns), foreign_keys pragma, synchronous mode tuning.
- fly.io / backup concerns (critical-8g1.5).

## Notes
No generated code (no migration, no .sql query), so no `just generate`. Not risky. Touches the same package as qki.5 / PR #26 but is not blocked by it.

title: Rulebooks reference: PHB + DMG as agent-readable docs in a private repo
description:
The user's request (2026-10-13, verbatim): "we should have the phb and the dmg in the repo in documentation in a format suitable for agents to refer to. ideally with some kind of indexing to avoid wasting tokens. what do you propose." Sources: https://archive.org/details/player-s-handbook-2nd-edition-2101 and https://archive.org/details/add2nddungeonmastersguidetsr2100

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- ceffo/critical is PUBLIC and the books are WotC copyright, so no rules text goes into critical. The converted text lives in a separate PRIVATE repo, ceffo/critical-rulebooks.
- critical worktrees reach it through a sibling clone at the fixed path ~/code/critical-rulebooks (no submodule: `git worktree add` doesn't init submodules). critical gets only a `just rulebooks` recipe and a pointer in AGENTS.md / docs/agent-workflow.md.
- The supervisor creates the repo (`gh repo create ceffo/critical-rulebooks --private`) and pushes the private repo's work straight to its `main` after its `check` passes. No PRs in the private repo. The critical item is a normal PR.
- The raw archive.org OCR (`*_djvu.txt`, plus the PHB `_page_numbers.json`) is committed under source/. PDFs are fetched on demand by a script, never committed.
- INDEX.md: one line per chapter/section/spell/table PLUS every entry from both printed book indexes, each resolved to `term | book p.N | path`. Agents grep it, never read it whole.
- No seed-shaped spell export: the vodabois scrape stays the app's spell catalog source of truth. PHB spell files carry their stat block as frontmatter only.
- Books in scope: the PHB and DMG only. The layout takes another <book>/ later without rework.
- Not MVP (Saturday hard cut): P3, outside critical-qki.

## Private repo gate (instead of `just validate`)

title: Create critical-rulebooks: OCR source, conversion script, PHB/DMG section files, INDEX.md with the printed indexes
description:
Create the private repo ceffo/critical-rulebooks and a reproducible conversion of the PHB and DMG (archive.org OCR) into section-sized Markdown files with a grep-able INDEX.md. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
See the parent epic. The supervisor runs `gh repo create ceffo/critical-rulebooks --private`, clones it to ~/code/critical-rulebooks and gives the developer a worktree of it. The developer commits there and the supervisor pushes to main once `check` passes (no PR).

## Current behaviour
Nothing exists. Supervisor's sample of the archive.org `*_djvu.txt` OCR (PHB ~1.5 MB, DMG ~1.2 MB): the prose is clean. Problems: line-break hyphenation ("unerr- ingly"), stray quotes ("Tenser’'s"), running headers/footers and page numbers inline, tables mangled. Both books have a printed index (term -> page). The PHB item also has `_page_numbers.json`.

## Key interfaces
- Repo layout: `source/` (raw djvu.txt + page_numbers.json, committed as downloaded), `scripts/` (convert, fetch-pdfs, check), `phb/chNN-<slug>/<NN>-<section-slug>.md` (or `phb/chNN-<slug>.md` when a chapter is small), `dmg/...` the same, `INDEX.md`, `README.md` (how to regenerate, how agents should use it).
- Each section file: a few thousand tokens at most; starts with `# <heading>` and a line `Source: PHB p.N-M`. Split at the book's own section headings, keep the book's wording.
- INDEX.md lines: `term | PHB p.N | phb/...md` (sorted, one entry per line, no prose). It contains every chapter and section heading plus every printed-index entry of both books, each resolved to the file holding that page. Unresolvable entries go to a list in README, never dropped silently.
- Cleanup: de-hyphenate across line breaks (keep real hyphens), normalise quotes, strip running headers/footers/page numbers (record page breaks as `<!-- p.N -->` comments so pages stay resolvable).
- Tables: this item leaves them as the OCR has them, fenced and marked `<!-- TABLE: unverified -->`. Item 3 replaces them.
- `scripts/check` as defined in the epic.
- Language/tooling: anything that runs offline on this machine (Python 3 stdlib preferred); no network in convert.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Private repo exists with source/, scripts/, README.md; the source files are byte-identical to archive.org's.
- [ ] Running the conversion twice gives identical output (`check` proves it).
- [ ] Every PHB and DMG chapter is split into section files, none over ~4k tokens (check reports the largest).
- [ ] No hyphenation artefacts or running headers in a sample of 10 random files (listed in the handoff).
- [ ] INDEX.md resolves every section heading and every printed-index entry of both books; unresolved ones listed in README with the reason.
- [ ] `grep -i surprise INDEX.md` and `grep -i thac0 INDEX.md` each give lines pointing at existing files.
- [ ] `check` passes.

## Out of scope
Per-spell files (item 2), hand-checked tables (item 3), anything in critical (item 4), other books, seed data.

## Notes
Not risky (docs/tooling, no app code). Sonnet. No generated code in critical.

title: One file per PHB spell (Wizard, Priest) with stat-block frontmatter, indexed
description:

title: Hand-checked PHB and DMG rule tables in tables/, indexed
description:
Replace the OCR-mangled rule tables of the PHB and DMG with hand-checked Markdown tables, verified against the PDF page images, in tables/, and index them. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- Hand-checked against the archive.org PDFs (fetched by scripts/fetch-pdfs, never committed). Opus: verifying OCR tables against page images is fiddly.
- Pushed by the supervisor to the private repo's main after `check` passes.
- Chained after item 2 only because both rewrite INDEX.md; no real data dependency.

## Current behaviour
After item 1 the tables are left as OCR text, fenced and marked `<!-- TABLE: unverified -->`.

## Key interfaces
- `tables/<book>-<slug>.md`, one table per file: `# <Table N: title>`, `Source: PHB p.N`, a Markdown table, footnotes as printed.
- Section files keep a one-line link to the table file instead of the OCR table.
- INDEX.md: one line per table, `Table N: <title> | PHB p.N | tables/phb-....md`.
- `check` gains: no `TABLE: unverified` marker left among the listed tables; every table file is linked from INDEX.md.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At least these tables are hand-checked against the page images: PHB ability score tables (Str, Dex, Con, Int, Wis, Cha), THAC0/combat progression, saving throws, XP and level progression per class group, spell progression (wizard, priest, bard), weapon tables (cost/weight/size/type/speed/damage), armour, movement/encumbrance; DMG attack matrices and saving throws, experience tables, magic item tables (random generation tables and XP/GP values).
- [ ] Every other table in both books is either checked or still carries the unverified marker, listed in README as unverified.
- [ ] The handoff lists each checked table with its page and any cell the OCR got wrong.
- [ ] `check` passes.

## Out of scope
Changing critical's seeds or rule_tables.json (if a mismatch with critical's seeds is found, report it to the supervisor for a separate item), other books.

## Notes
Not risky (no app code). Opus. Blocked by item 2 (INDEX.md conflict only).

title: Point critical's agents at the rulebooks: just rulebooks recipe and the INDEX-first usage rule
description:
Make the private rulebooks clone available to every critical worktree and tell agents how to use it cheaply. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- Sibling clone at the fixed path ~/code/critical-rulebooks, shared by every worktree (no submodule).
- critical is PUBLIC: no rules text, no excerpts, only the path, the recipe and the usage rule.

## Current behaviour
No reference to the rulebooks; agents answer rules questions from docs/backend.md, the ADRs and memory.

## Key interfaces
- `just rulebooks`: clones git@github.com:ceffo/critical-rulebooks.git to ~/code/critical-rulebooks if it is missing, otherwise `git pull --ff-only`. Prints a clear message and exits non-zero without access (e.g. a public user without the private repo); it never runs as part of `just validate` or `just dev`.
- AGENTS.md + docs/agent-workflow.md (a short "Rulebooks" section; agent-workflow.md is where the agents read project specifics): for rules questions, `grep -i '<term>' ~/code/critical-rulebooks/INDEX.md` first, open only the file it names, never read whole chapters or INDEX.md whole. If the clone is missing, run `just rulebooks`; if that fails, say so instead of guessing the rule. The PHB/DMG text is a reference; the project's decided rules (ADRs in docs/adr, user rulings) win where they differ.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `just rulebooks` clones when absent and fast-forwards when present (try both by hand); it fails cleanly without access.
- [ ] AGENTS.md and docs/agent-workflow.md hold the pointer and usage rule above, no book text.
- [ ] `just validate` passes.

## Out of scope
The private repo's contents (items 1-3), any CI access to the private repo.

## Notes
Not risky (docs/tooling). Sonnet. Blocked by item 1 (the repo and INDEX.md must exist so the recipe and the grep example work). It touches different repos from items 2 and 3, so it can run in parallel with them.
